title: Isandro and the Well
premise: Odile Lockridge, a pest controller who prides herself on explaining everything with biology and bad wiring, is hired to investigate strange activity at her estranged grandmother's farmhouse. She discovers the house has been 'inviting' something in for generations—a presence that manifests as an extra chair in every photograph—and that her grandmother made a bargain before her death: a life for a harvest, due when the harvest moon rises. As Odile digs through family records, she learns she was the promised payment all along, traded away before birth by parents desperate to escape the debt. With help from the grandmother's ragtag neighbors—who have quietly protected each other from the well's hunger for decades—Odile chooses to break the cycle rather than pay it, sealing the well at dawn but losing the farmhouse, her denial, and nearly her life; she ends not alone, but adopted into the found family that refused to let her be taken.
about_author: Mara Nakamura is the pen name of a former rural insurance adjuster who spent years documenting claims no one could explain away. They write horror about stubborn people in old houses, and live somewhere with very deep groundwater.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: POV Odile. A routine pest-control call leads Odile to her estranged grandmother's farmhouse—grandmother recently dead, house inherited by nobody, yet someone keeps paying for exterminations. She finds droppings that don't match any species and claw marks on the inside of the well cover. Emotional beat: irritation masking grief she refuses to name.

chapters.title: One Chair Too Many
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Sorting her grandmother's photos to settle the estate, Odile notices every image after 1987 contains an extra wooden chair where none should be—closer to the camera in each successive decade. The last photo, dated last month, shows the chair facing the front door. Emotional beat: rational explanations begin to fail, and dread takes root.

chapters.title: The Neighbors Who Stay
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The neighboring farmers—the Okafor brothers and widow Hettie Marsh—arrive uninvited with salt, iron nails, and casseroles, treating the situation like a scheduled event. They reveal every Lockridge has faced the harvest moon, and every one of them had neighbors who helped. Emotional beat: wary warmth; the first hint of found family.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept Below
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In the cellar, behind shelves of preserved fruit, Odile finds her grandmother's ledger: dates, offerings, and a column labeled 'owed.' The final entry names a debtor born under a waning moon—her own birthday. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into fear as duty becomes personal.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Things escalate: wet fingerprints on the inside of windows, the extra chair now physically present in the kitchen each morning, moved an inch closer to her bedroom nightly. Hettie explains the entity doesn't haunt—it negotiates. Emotional beat: Odile's skepticism collapses into grim acceptance.

chapters.title: The Bargain Before Birth
chapters.summary: POV alternating Odile and ledger excerpts. Through letters, Odile reconstructs how her parents traded her unborn self to escape the farm, and how her grandmother spent thirty years paying interest to keep the debt deferred. Emotional beat: rage at her parents softening toward the grandmother who tried to buy her freedom.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The moon swells full and orange; the well uncovers itself, and the chair sits at the head of the table set for one. The Okafors and Hettie arrive armed with the only plan they've ever known: give it what it wants and survive the night. Emotional beat: terror braided with defiance.

chapters.title: Invited In
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The entity speaks through the house itself, offering Odile the same deal her parents took: walk away, forget, let it take someone else someday. It shows her the loneliness it feeds on—hers included. Emotional beat: temptation; love against duty turns inward as she must choose which debt to honor.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Instead of paying or fleeing, Odile renegotiates: she offers the thing its own contract, binding it to the well forever using the ledger, salt, and her own blood as signature. The house fights back through the long dark hours until dawn. Climax: she holds out until sunrise, barely alive, the debt annulled.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV Odile, epilogue weeks later. The farmhouse is condemned and sold for salvage; the well is filled with concrete and sunflowers. At Hettie's table, set with four places, Odile finally sits down to eat with people who stayed. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—family chosen, denial shed, the chair left empty on purpose.
